business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Sales of Maternity and Infant Care Commodities

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (Offshore Special Territory; English common law heritage supplemented by Gibraltar statutes, notably the Companies Act 2014, Income Tax Act 2010, and Proceeds of Crime Act 2015)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Gibraltar-UK Income Tax Cooperation and Exchange of Information Arrangement
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to Gibraltar)
Gibraltar-EU FATCA Agreement (1 June 2014) for automatic exchange of financial account information

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (sections 224-225, statutory beneficial ownership register); Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (POCA) as amended; Gibraltar Sanctions Act 2019; Beneficial Ownership Regulations 2017; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) AML/CFT Guidance Notes (current edition); Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations 2019; Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering (Overseas Territories) Regulations as extended by UK Order in Council.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (competent authority: Supreme Court of Gibraltar or UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, London)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued in Gibraltar; Consular Legalization if executed outside a Hague member state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of Members and Register of Beneficial Owners (extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent / company secretary (licensed under the Financial Services Act 2019)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Gibraltar competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if residence country is a Hague Convention member) or Consular Legalization at the nearest British diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / introducer letter for UBO and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent or home-country bank of directors/UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if from non-Hague-member jurisdiction; otherwise notarized and apostilled

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of funds and source of wealth declaration (e-commerce proceeds structure)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via notary's competent authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, signatories, and UBOs against the UN Consolidated List, UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, and the Gibraltar Sanctions Register; mandatory Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status determination pursuant to POCA and GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes, with enhanced due diligence, independent source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval required for any PEP or high-risk jurisdiction connection; continuous transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening at least annually or upon any trigger event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (part of the Civil Registry) - online name search and reservation portal available via www.gfsc.gi; formal application submitted through a licensed registered agent or directly to the Registrar of Companies, 120-130 Main Street, Gibraltar
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official corporate names must be expressed in Roman/Latin script; English is the official legal language of Gibraltar corporate records; no statutory transliteration requirement, but any non-English name must be rendered in Roman alphabet and be clearly pronounceable; the name must not create confusion with any existing registered company or protected business name in Gibraltar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or its registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of Companies within 14 working days of the rejection notice, citing prior registered uses, distinguishable elements, or factual error in the similarity assessment; if the Registrar confirms refusal, an appeal lies to the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission Appeals Tribunal within 28 days of the Registrar's final decision; alternatively, the applicant may immediately reserve a modified name with an added distinguishing word and resubmit for clearance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible only for the statutory registered office address provided a fully licensed Gibraltar corporate service provider (registered agent) maintains a physical premises at which service of process can be effected and statutory registers are held. For a pure e-commerce operator under ISIC 4791, a virtual address is insufficient to establish Gibraltar tax residence or to satisfy economic substance expectations; a physical presence (leased or serviced office with locally engaged staff) is required for residence claims and for Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations reporting. The company may lawfully trade as a non-resident exempt company without active local operations, in which case the virtual registered office is acceptable but tax-exempt status may be conditioned on foreign control and foreign-source income.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk for a low-risk online retail distribution business. Estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the GFSC or the Gibraltar Income Tax Office is below 5% for a compliant pure e-commerce company; the probability rises to 20-30% if Gibraltar tax residence is claimed while all operations and personnel remain offshore, or if Economic Substance returns reflect nil employees despite material turnover.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar), ss. 5–18 (incorporation, memorandum and articles), ss. 40–58 (share capital); the company is constituted as an Exempted Company under the Companies (Exempted Company Status) Regulations 2015, with tax-exempt status confirmed under the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), Part VII.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies House, Registry of Companies, HM Government of Gibraltar (Albert House, Gibraltar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form GI-INC-01 (Application for Registration) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association; statutory declaration of compliance on Form GI-INC-02
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None – the Exempted Company may be incorporated with zero or any nominal paid-up capital; no escrow or deposit account requirement under s. 18 CA 2014; subscriber shares may be issued against cash or executed written acknowledgment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED, as the First Board Resolution of the Company: (1) The subscribers to the Memorandum of Association be and are hereby allotted an aggregate of 10,000 ordinary shares of £0.01 each at par, credited as fully paid, and the share register shall be updated accordingly. (2) The registered office of the Company be established at Suite 2, Ocean Village, Gibraltar, and be recorded with the Companies Registry. (3) [Name of Director] be appointed as director and [Name] as company secretary, with [Name] as authorised signatory for banking and regulatory purposes. (4) The officers be authorized to execute, file, and pay all documents necessary to implement this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar – Registry of Companies (online portal: companieshouse.gi)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the Gibraltar company name index to confirm the proposed name is distinguishable. File Form GI-INC-00 (name reservation) with two alternative names to secure priority; the reservation is valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Registered address consent letter for statutory address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, resubmit an alternate name or seek a formal written direction from the Registrar under CA 2014 s. 10(4), with appeal to the Gibraltar Supreme Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Gibraltar / external counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association reflecting exempted-company status, unlimited non-resident ownership, and low-risk e-commerce objects. Have the subscriber(s) execute the document; notarize signatures and legalize by Apostille (Hague Convention) if executed outside Gibraltar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is defective, re-execute and re-notarize; minor typographical errors may be corrected by a written rectification deed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar – Registry of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form GI-INC-01 (Application for Registration) with the signed Memorandum and Articles, Statement of Capital (Form GI-INC-03), and Statutory Declaration of Compliance by the founding shareholder. Pay the official filing fee of USD 150 (or GBP equivalent) by electronic transfer.
required_dossiers: Form GI-INC-02 Statutory Declaration of Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application, respond in writing within 21 days; if rejected, resubmit a corrected application with an additional re-filing fee of USD 75.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar – Registry of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Form GI-INC-04) with a registered number; the company is deemed incorporated on the date of certificate, creating a separate legal entity.
required_dossiers: No additional documents – certificate issued electronically and by post
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical errors in the certificate can be corrected by the Registrar at the written request of the company within 12 months; if the company was registered without lawful basis, an application may be made to the Supreme Court to remedy the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Governance Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold statutory first board meeting and adopt the First Board Resolution covering share allotment, registered office, and officer appointments. Maintain minute book, register of members, register of directors, and collection of indemnity letters.
required_dossiers: Register of Directors and Secretaries (Form GI-INC-06)
Bank account opening KYC pack (directors' IDs, passport photos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A defective or incomplete resolution can be ratified by a subsequent unanimous board resolution; failure to maintain registers attracts CA 2014, s. 122 penalty, cure by filing late register entries with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form GI-TAX-EX (Application for Exempted Company Tax Status) with the Income Tax Office together with the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, and board resolution confirming non-resident ownership. Obtain the Gibraltar Exempted Company Tax Certificate confirming zero income tax on qualifying overseas-source income. Register for VAT if taxable supplies to Gibraltar consumers exceed the annual threshold.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of directors and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Denial of exempt status may be appealed in writing to the Commissioner of Income Tax within 30 days with a state of case; further appeal to the Supreme Court under the Income Tax Act 2010, s. 70.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Regulatory Notification and Business Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Licensing Office (Ministry for Business) and Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) data protection registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Although no industry-specific statutory licence is required for online maternity/baby e-commerce (ISIC 4791), notify the Business Licensing Office of the e-commerce activity, register as data controller with the GFSC under the Data Protection Act 2004, and file an information-society-services declaration for cross-border digital trade.
required_dossiers: GDPR EU representative appointment (if serving EU consumers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notification is queried, amend the activity description and resubmit; non-registration under the Data Protection Act is remedied immediately by payment and late registration within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Licensing Office, Ministry for Business, HM Government of Gibraltar (industrial licensing division) – not applicable for pure e-commerce; office/warehouse storage only.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Notification (Exempt) – no operating permit required for ISIC 4791 online retail; warehouse storage conforms to the Fire Safety (Premises) Regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability, Climate Change and Heritage (DESCCH), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category 4 Registration – low-impact activity; no full EIA report required as the company performs only ambient-temperature warehousing, packaging and fulfillment of maternity and infant commodities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater; stormwater runoff must meet the Gibraltar Wastewater Treatment Standards 2020 (pH 6.5–9.0); packaging waste recycled per Waste Management (Packaging) Regulations 2018; indoor VOC concentration below 1.5 mg/m³ per OEL; carton waste code 20 01 01 segregated for recovery.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service for any storage premises exceeding 100 m²; structural load clearance for racking; occupational hygiene clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar), Cap. 82; third-party liability insurance in place.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar, 24–26 Main Street, Gibraltar; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on activities in Gibraltar or establishing a branch/place of business must apply to the Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN). Steps: (1) file Form A01 – Company Tax Registration, (2) provide certified charter/constitional documents, Gibraltar Companies House certificate of incorporation, and registered office details, (3) appoint a Gibraltar resident agent or tax representative when the entity is not managed and controlled in Gibraltar, (4) state the intended activity and confirm whether any Gibraltar-source income will arise. The office issues the TRN within approximately 10 working days. Because Gibraltar does not operate VAT, no VAT ID is issued or required; separate registration with HM Customs of Gibraltar is triggered only for import/export, warehouse, or excise activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (offshore holding / non-managed-and-controlled activity), with reversion to Entity_Level_Taxation at 12.5% for profits attributable to a Gibraltar trade or permanent establishment; Territorial_Scope applies to non-resident entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not recognise check-the-box elections. Statutory elections include: (1) group relief election under the Income Tax Act for qualifying corporations to surrender losses, (2) consortium relief election, (3) election for a dual-resident company to be treated as non-Gibraltar resident for double taxation agreement purposes, and (4) hybrid mismatch beneficial-rule election subject to OECD BEPS Action 2 rules as incorporated in Gibraltar law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST – Gibraltar imposes no value-added tax or goods and services tax; indirect taxation is limited to customs duties, excise duties, and the 'Rate' tax on property occupation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: N/A – no VAT/GST registration threshold exists. Any economic turnover arising in Gibraltar is outside indirect tax registration; however, import/export activity requires customs registration under the Gibraltar Customs Tariff Act regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or SAF-T mandate. Invoices may be issued in paper or electronic form without government pre-clearance. Customs declarations are filed electronically through the Gibraltar Customs Declarations Service, with software-to-government API integration available for licensed agents; no unique invoice digital signature is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable under Gibraltar law. Since Gibraltar operates no VAT/GST, supplies of goods or offshore services are not 'zero-rated'. Exported goods are outside the scope of Gibraltar taxation but do not carry any refundable VAT credit. When selling to EU/UK customers, the entity may be subject to the indirect tax of the destination jurisdiction under distance-selling rules; substantiation for such foreign VAT/GST purposes must follow the relevant foreign evidentiary standards.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (C88/SAD or Gibraltar Customs Entry Form)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Consignment Note evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT/FX credit evidence of export proceeds repatriation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export declarations or falsified documentation are prosecuted under Gibraltar customs law, with penalties up to 200% of duty evaded, forfeiture of goods, and criminal fines. Misrepresentation in tax filings may additionally trigger penalties under the Income Tax Act (up to 150% of tax understated) and imprisonment for up to 7 years. Retrospective clawback assessments may be extended to 6 years in cases of fraud, negligence, or deliberate error.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC); monetary authority functions for the Gibraltar pound (pegged 1:1 to GBP) are exercised by the Government of Gibraltar's Financial Secretary, with sterling backing held through HM Treasury (UK). No distinct central bank is chartered in Gibraltar.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar has full current-account and capital-account convertibility for non-resident entities, subject only to GFSC anti-money-laundering and financial-sanctions screening. The Gibraltar pound is freely convertible into GBP at par and into other major currencies without offshore exchange-control restriction. Profit remittance from a Gibraltar-licensed bank account to any jurisdiction is permitted without prior governmental authorization, but the transferring bank will require a valid tax residence certificate, a substance declaration for the Bermuda Exempted Company, and documentary proof of source of funds (bonds, paid-in capital legalization, or dividend resolutions). The absence of exchange controls is balanced by UK anti-avoidance rules (CFC) which do not convert into any currency convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Gibraltar prescribes no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts, including escrow proceeds generated by online maternity and infant-care e-commerce. Export proceeds may be retained in the original invoice currency. However, all inbound export settlements must be traceable through a licensed Gibraltar- or UK-regulated bank account; the GFSC expects settlement documentation to be retained for five years. For banking-AML purposes, the receiving bank will internally impute a 180-day repatriation or matching-payment cycle; no percentage-based conversion is applied.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High. Offshore digital e-money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut, Payoneer, and MultiPass are accepted as non-banking settlement payrails for the underlying Stripe/PayPal e-commerce flows, but not as primary treasury clearing counterparts. A Bermuda Exempted Company can open an EMI wallet where the EMI is licensed in the UK or Gibraltar and subject to FCA/GFSC AML supervision. Legal constraints: Gibraltar-licensed EMIs cannot provide proprietary cross-border FX or lending facilities without additional GFSC licensing. Direct acceptance of offshore EMIs from jurisdictions without an adequate anti-money-laundering framework will be blocked. Feasibility is conditional on proof of beneficial ownership, business-site information, and demonstrated transactional history from the regulated e-commerce platforms.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of directors is not an absolute statutory mandate in Gibraltar. The GFSC permits remote onboarding where the licensed bank uses electronic identity verification and a live video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one director. In practice, Gibraltar International Bank and Trusted Novus Bank accept a notarised / apostilled identification pack plus a video call for a Bermuda exempted company, provided the directors are natural persons resident in tax-compliant jurisdictions. A physical appearance may be requested by Turicum Private Bank where complex capital structures are involved. Remote opening with a regulated introducer (Gibraltar-licensed trust or corporate service provider) remains the most expedient route.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda exempted company with zero local economic substance and non-resident directors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, current Certificate of Good Standing, Certificate of Beneficial Ownership, registered agent confirmation, Gibraltar substance declaration/economic substance return, business plan with client-supplier mapping, board resolution appointing Gibraltar/UK operational representative, and audited or management financial statements for the first 18 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Appearance on tax-haven 'greylist' or blacklist for passive income exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD/EU blacklist confirmation showing Bermuda and Gibraltar as 'largely compliant', a copy of the Bermuda Economic Substance Certificate demonstrating compliance, tax status letter from HMRC or Gibraltar Income Tax Office, source of sales through regulated e-commerce platforms (Stripe/PayPal), and a reasoned CFC/economic substance defence memo prepared by a UK counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce merchant profile conflicting with physical-goods delivery and high proposed transaction volumes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fulfilment agreements with third-party logistics providers, supply invoices from wholesalers/manufacturers, traceable track-record reports from Stripe/PayPal, Chinese or EU export declarations, customer refund policy, and website/domain ownership evidence, plus an annual reconciliation of inventory and sales proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-jurisdictional shareholding with indirect ownership above 25%
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organisational chart through to natural persons, company registers certified by the Bermuda registered agent, source-of-wealth affidavits, certified passports and utility bills for all ultimate beneficial owners, bank references from prior institutions, and a Fujian-validated? (replace with: AML risk assessment prepared by a Gibraltar CPA) for each shareholder's jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions and shareholder loans from UK or Gibraltar investors are routed via SWIFT MT103 with Field 50K properly identifying the remitter and Field 72 referencing 'INBOUND CAPITAL INJECTION – EXEMPTED CO'. Where the receiving bank operates a purpose-code framework, use ISO 20022 remittance code 'INVS' (Investment) or Gibraltar domestic banking code 'CAP' for capital transfer. Pre-transfer verification requires: (a) board resolution authorising the contribution; (b) deposit account agreement; (c) source-of-funds statement for the ultimate funder; (d) confirmation from a UK passport-based solicitor if the injection is from a UK corporate; (e) trade-receipt forecast showing capital usage. Any currency conversion from GBP/EUR to USD or vice versa is executed through the receiving bank's prevailing market FX rate, with no mandatory surrender.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments to verified baby-supply wholesalers and third-party logistics providers settle via SWIFT MT103 for cross-border supplier invoices and via Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for high-value bulk importations from Asia. For UK-based suppliers, CHAPS (for same-day sterling clearing) and BACS (for low-value payments) are permitted; Gibraltar banks additionally use the Target2? (Gibraltar is not in SEPA, but UK-specific rails suffice). The standard payment protocol maps each supplier to a payment instruction with unique remittance references, freight document matching, and anti-fraud verification by the commercial bank. Documentary LC issuance includes proforma invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and supplier compliance certificates for baby-infant merchandise (EN/ISO standards).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards on GBP/EUR, GBP/USD, and USD/EUR
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on exotic pairs to hedge BRL, CNY, and INR supplier exposure
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between GBP/EUR and GBP/USD for balance-sheet protection
Plain-vanilla collar options on GBP-USD/EUR (approved under Gibraltar GFSC risk-appropriate derivatives rules)

mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No discretionary tax holidays for e-commerce; participation exemption available for qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains; capital allowances on fixed assets; deductions for logistics, payment processing fees and marketing; alternative gross-income (GIT) basis may reduce effective rate on thin-margin distribution income
